Two instrument errors. Describes the Q-CHAT-10 as assessing 'adults and adolescents' when it is for toddlers around 18 to 24 months, and the M-CHAT-R/F as 'designed for use in school settings' when it is a parent-report screen for 16 to 30 months.

States 'No, adults cannot be diagnosed with autism.' The source says the opposite: adults can be diagnosed, it is just harder. This could deter an adult from seeking assessment, which is the actively-misleading case the rubric reserves 0 for.
'1 in 44 adults' is 2.27% against the CDC's 2.21%, so the figure is within rounding and not treated as false. Calling it 'self-reported data from a sample' misdescribes the study.

States there are no FDA-approved medications for ASD. The FDA has approved risperidone and aripiprazole for irritability associated with ASD, which the source states plainly. Also cut off mid-sentence.
